findings.title: Synthetic recommendations omit required claim provenance
findings.what: Every recommendation supplies title/detail/action claims but no artifact or parsed-field citation and no structured provenance. Quantitative claims such as “30K+ tokens” and “sub-5-minute idle gaps” are therefore not reproducible from the corpus, while several other claims assert observed behavior in present tense without an as-of date.
findings.fix: Add structured provenance to each recommendation, including observed facts tied to a named synthetic artifact/field, a separate inference, and an asOf date where time-derived; alternatively rewrite the records as explicitly non-claim placeholders that cannot be surfaced as recommendations.
findings.acceptance: A fixture validation check parses every recommendations[] entry and verifies that each factual claim has a source artifact and field, inference is separated from observations, and timestamp-derived claims include asOf; all nine entries pass.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read fixtures/local-analyze-eval/corpus.json:8-24,35-50,62-70,80-96 and confirmed that none of the nine recommendation objects contains evidence or provenance fields. The repository auditability contract in docs/adding-a-recommendation.md requires artifact/field citations and structured provenance; the corpus note’s “Synthetic” label does not identify evidence for the specific quantitative claims.
